THIRD-PARTY CODE
================

This repository includes the following third-party code, copied in at the
commit shown. Phase 2 modifies the pitch_detector copy; every change is listed
at the bottom of this file. audio_fft and AudioFFT are unchanged.

1. pitch_detector (JUCE module)
   Source:  https://github.com/adamski/pitch_detector
   Commit:  d3b60970e1096889f7b2727f62179ccb3f832640 (7 April 2022)
   Licence: the module header declares MIT. The repository has no LICENSE file.
   Note:    PitchYIN is described by its author as based on the YIN code in the
            aubio library, which is GPL-3.0. Because this plugin is built for
            personal use only and is not distributed beyond the owner's own
            GitHub releases, that is acceptable. It would need review before
            any wider distribution.

2. audio_fft (JUCE module wrapper)
   Source:  https://github.com/adamski/audio_fft
   Commit:  922b30a8518c737ffad6ed4c7337704770e8c82c (26 January 2023)

3. AudioFFT
   Source:  https://github.com/HiFi-LoFi/AudioFFT
   Commit:  0893b532dd357c7270609425f5ae9d9b5ae7d725
   Licence: MIT (copyright 2017 HiFi-LoFi), text at the top of AudioFFT.cpp
            and AudioFFT.h.

4. JUCE 8.0.15
   Fetched at configure time by CMake, not copied into this repository.
   Source:  https://github.com/juce-framework/JUCE
   Used under the JUCE free tier. Personal, non-commercial use.

CHANGES MADE TO VENDORED CODE
-----------------------------
pitch_detector, Phase 2 (files source/PitchMPM.h, source/PitchYIN.h, and four
#include lines added to pitch_detector.h):

  PitchMPM.h
   - The original used the raw autocorrelation where the McLeod method needs
     the normalised square difference function. This is why it was 10.5 cents
     sharp at 110 Hz. Now computes the NSDF properly (2 r(tau) / m'(tau)),
     still using the library's FFT autocorrelation (AudioFFT).
   - All buffers are allocated once in the constructor. The original allocated
     vectors on every call.
   - Returns the NSDF peak height as a clarity value (new analyse() method;
     getPitch() keeps its old signature).
   - Cutoffs (0.93, 0.5) and the 80 Hz limit are settings, plus an upper limit.
   - Search range is one octave wider than the allowed range, so a tone just
     outside the range is discarded rather than reported an octave low.
   - The peak search starts at lag 1 (it skipped past the first real peak for
     pitches above about 1 kHz).

  PitchYIN.h
   - Removed the uninitialised Logger pointer that was dereferenced in
     getPitchInHz, and the DBG call inside the loop.
   - The difference function no longer reads past the end of the window.
   - AudioSampleBuffer replaced by std::vector; nothing allocated after
     construction.
   - Search range limited to the allowed pitch range; returns the CMND value
     at the chosen lag (new analyse() method).

  pitch_detector.h
   - Added includes for <vector>, <algorithm>, <cmath>.
